stem: A unit measures staff hand-hygiene adherence by direct observation. Which limitation should the nurse recognize when interpreting the observed compliance rate?

options.A: Staff may improve hand-hygiene behavior when they know or suspect they are being observed, which can bias the measured rate upward
options.B: Direct observation cannot be used to assess hand-hygiene adherence in health care settings
options.C: Direct observation measures only surgical hand antisepsis and cannot capture routine hand-hygiene opportunities
options.D: Observation completely eliminates sampling and observer-related measurement bias

rationale: CDC literature on hand-hygiene compliance monitoring identifies the Hawthorne effect as a recognized concern with observation-based measurement: behavior can change in the presence of observation, potentially making observed adherence appear better than usual practice. Direct observation remains an established auditing method, so B and C are incorrect, and observation does not eliminate other sources of measurement bias.
educational_objective: Recognize the Hawthorne effect as a limitation of direct observation when interpreting hand-hygiene compliance data.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) — Emerging Infectious Diseases
source_document_title: Reduction of Healthcare-Associated Infections by Exceeding High Compliance with Hand Hygiene Practices
source_version_date: Volume 22, Number 9, September 2016; current CDC-hosted article accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: The Study/Discussion of compliance measurement: hand-hygiene compliance measurements have concerns associated with interobserver variation, sampling bias, and the Hawthorne effect; study design discusses controlling/using the Hawthorne effect
source_claim_supported: The Hawthorne effect is a recognized limitation/measurement concern when hand-hygiene compliance is assessed through observation.

blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand-hygiene auditing / evaluation of staff infection-control practice
correction_summary: Removed the managerial narrative and made the item a direct interpretation of hand-hygiene audit data. Retained Safety and Infection Prevention and Control after confirming NCSBN explicitly includes hand hygiene and evaluation of staff infection-control precautions. Replaced weak distractors with realistic errors about observation-based monitoring.
audit_findings: A is the recognized Hawthorne-bias limitation. B contradicts CDC/WHO use of direct observation for hand-hygiene monitoring; C incorrectly restricts observation to surgical scrub; D incorrectly claims observation eliminates bias. One best answer remains and the blueprint is directly supported by the 2026 Test Plan.
